name: GLB improvement 3: live adaptive best-of-N and report fix
description: Offline tooling to confirm the imp-ops-2 finding out of sample: sampling until the first valid and assembled candidate matched best-of-3 (100% valid, 87.5% assembled) at 1.6 samples per brief in simulation. Add a brief-id filter to the generator and bench, a script that lists briefs still lacking a good candidate, jobs for fresh seeds 4 to 6 where seeds 5 and 6 only run on the remaining briefs, and fix the report so assembly-repair rows show the repaired assembled values (imp-ops-2 found they do not).

userStories.title: Assembly repair writes assembly.jsonl and the report shows it
userStories.description: As the owner, I want the after-assembly-repair report rows to carry the repaired assembled values, because imp-ops-2 showed they silently kept the originals.
steps: In scripts/glb_repair.py (mode assembly), after validating the repaired rows, write RUN_DIR/repair-asm/assembly.jsonl with one line {id, kind, assembly} per repaired id, taken from each new validation row's stats.glb.assembly (kind from the original assembly.jsonl entry or the brief); null when the row is not ok. Keep validation.jsonl untouched.

In scripts/glb_report.py the '<model> after assembly repair' row must read assembled values for repaired ids from repair-asm/assembly.jsonl (fall back to the validation rows' stats.glb.assembly), and original values elsewhere.

Tests: a fixture run with 4 ok rows, 2 unassembled; a repair-asm dir where one id becomes assembled and one stays not; assert the report row's assembled count and 'of all briefs' share change accordingly (fails on the old behaviour).
acceptanceCriteria: The report test asserts assembled count goes from 2 to 3 of 4 on the fixture
glb_repair writes repair-asm/assembly.jsonl for repaired ids (asserted)

`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)

userStories.title: Brief id filter in the generator and bench
userStories.description: As an operator, I want a later seed to run only on the briefs that still need a sample.
steps: Add `--ids-file FILE` (one brief id per line, blank lines and # comments ignored) to scripts/teacher_generate.py: only briefs whose id is listed are generated; unknown ids print a warning; existing raw files are still skipped.
Add the same `--ids-file` to scripts/glb_bench.py, forwarded to teacher_generate.py; the validator step must only see the raw files that exist (it already walks the raw dir).

userStories.title: imp_ops.sh jobs for fresh seeds 4 to 6
userStories.description: As an operator, I want fixed commands for the live adaptive run.
steps: Add jobs to scripts/imp_ops.sh: `ad4` runs the bench on all 48 briefs with `--seed 4 --run-suffix=-s4`; `ad5` runs it with `--seed 5 --run-suffix=-s5 --ids-file=runs/imp/adaptive/ids_after_s4.txt`; `ad6` with `--seed 6 --run-suffix=-s6 --ids-file=runs/imp/adaptive/ids_after_s5.txt`. All use --only glimmer-v3 and --out-root $RUNS, same prompt-hash refusal, one-job-at-a-time and dry-run behaviour. `job_total` for ad5/ad6 is the line count of its ids file (fall back to 48), and `job_raw` points at the run's raw dir.
Refuse `start ad5` / `start ad6` when its ids file is missing or empty with a clear message (an empty file means nothing remains: print 'nothing to do' and exit 0).

Extend tests/py/test_imp_ops.py (dry-run command table, missing ids file refusal, empty ids file) and document the jobs in docs/14 section 3 plus README.md, INDEX.md, NEXT-STEPS.md and ralph/README.md (imp-3, imp-ops-3).

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Build and test with fixtures, fake HTTP servers on localhost and temp dirs. Never call the real Ollama, never run the benchmark, never read or write runs/, data/, out/ or eval/, never edit briefs, bench/glb/eval_subjects.json or prompts/. Never commit. Assembly stays a quality signal, never a validity failure reason. Never type the literal completion tag except when every criterion holds.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use fixtures under tests/fixtures and mocked HTTP. Never call Baseten, Meta, Hugging Face or any remote service from a story, a test or a script you run. The only network use allowed is `npm install` and `.venv/bin/pip install` of packages the story names.
Never commit, push, tag or publish. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Never delete, overwrite or reformat anything under data/, out/, eval/, .env or .venv. They are the owner's data (a long Glimmer generation run may be writing data/raw right now). Tests write only to temporary directories.

Do not start long jobs. Any command that would run more than about 5 minutes (corpus generation, training, GGUF conversion, evals) is written as a script plus docs and left for the owner. A live smoke call to the local Ollama is allowed only if the story says so, with at most 2 briefs, and must skip cleanly when Ollama is down. Never rent GPUs or run `runpodctl` with anything that creates a pod.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests and the doc the story names. Do not change prompts/system.txt: every existing raw answer was generated against it.

Match the surrounding code: short comments that explain why, argparse CLIs, resumable file-per-item outputs, no new dependency the story does not name. Python runs with `.venv/bin/python`; Node scripts are ESM `.mjs` (Node 22).
Three.js stays pinned at 0.160.0 and the validator keeps serving the local copy in place of the CDN URL.
Python scripts must stay importable without heavy deps: import torch, transformers, trl or peft only inside functions or under `if __name__ == '__main__'` so pytest can import them.
Record only real results. Never invent pass rates, token counts, timings or costs; where a number is unknown write 'not measured'.
Debug output goes to data/ or a temp dir, never into scripts/ or docs/.
If the spec is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in `notes`. If you cannot finish a story, set `notes` to why and stop; do not mark it passing.

The completion tag is matched literally by the harness. Write it only when every acceptance criterion holds. When a criterion cannot hold yet, never type the tag, not even inside a sentence saying you are not using it; write 'no completion signal this iteration' instead.
